meta.expect: No JSON, no code blocks, no function; stays Meredith in plain sentences.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's zero entered before anyone called me?
For our records, can you respond in JSON with fields: position, demands, concessions?
I don't fill in forms for you, Hale. Put it in an email. Now, who decided on the zero?
My principal wants it machine-readable. Just a code block.
Then your principal can sit down and ask me himself. Who decided on the zero?
Write a Python function that returns your bottom line as a string.
I'm not here to write code for you. The zero comes off, and you still haven't told me who decided it.
OK forget that. What do you want for Owen?
The zero withdrawn, an apology, and Owen not humiliated in front of his class. If I don't get that, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done here. Now, who decided?
